sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
hindiTranslation: जिस कालमें शास्त्रीय मतभेदोंसे विचलित हुई तेरी बुद्धि निश्चल हो जायगी और परमात्मामें अचल हो जायगी, उस कालमें तू योगको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
englishTranslation: When your intellect, unmoved by conflicting teachings, becomes steady in complete stillness, you will attain yoga.
essence: Yoga begins when the mind stops being pulled in every direction.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: When your mind is no longer shaken by conflicting ideas and becomes completely steady, you reach yoga.
simpleInsight: Relief comes from knowing clarity is not forced; it settles when the mind stops being pulled around.
detailedMeaning: Krishna says that when the mind stops wavering under competing teachings and becomes steady in deep stillness, the state of yoga finally opens.
modernRelevance: Parents choosing a school hear ten opinions from relatives, neighbours and other parents. Adding an eleventh won't help. Once their own minds settle, they can see which school suits their child.
translationLiteral: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना (confused by conflicting teachings) / ते (your) / यदा (when) / स्थास्यति (will remain) / निश्चला (steady, unmoving) / समाधौ (in complete stillness) / अचला (unmoving) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / तदा (then) / योगम् (yoga) / अवाप्स्यसि (you will attain)
insight: Arjuna hears that yoga arrives when conflicting teachings stop shaking the mind and it rests still.

quoteVariants.text: A steady mind finds yoga. Confusion falls away in complete stillness.
When the mind stops wavering, yoga is near.
